content: Hi everyone! I have taken an interest in helping with the thermodynamic module of physlean.
Together with @Mitchell Scheffer we just issued our very first PR, about formalizing adiabatic transformations in the ideal gas
Our (tentative) next step will be to fomalize the ideal gas. We'll probably build a structure for it, but we'd love to know if the community has better ideas!

Hi, it's great to see this !
FYI you may be interested in this work in progress attempt to formalize Lieb-Yngvason. Of course it is a completely different approach, and I think PhysLean should have both, but it may help to see how to derive the axioms/assumptions you will have to make in your ideal gas structure.

Thank you for sending this, I didn't know about it. Yes, we should have both. Morally, what Lieb-Yngvason did was proving a bunch of things that are needed for a thermodynamic entropy to exist. While obviously I'll be assuming a bunch of properties of the entropy, as per Callen's axioms. It'd be great to find the proper way to connect these two approaches, although I'm not entirely sure how.

Hi all, I've opened a PR that links to the discussion happening in this thread:
https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/pull/1365

@Matteo Cipollina I spent some time working through the repo you linked here, and
you've covered substantial ground. I've used a lot of your ideas in my PR but haven't yet
added you as an author — please let me know and I'll be happy to make that change.

I'd also really appreciate your comments on the PR. The goal was to add something to Physlib
that would let us develop Callen-style macroscopic thermodynamics, hopefully port over your
work to finish the formalization of Lieb–Yngvason in Physlib, and, longer term, formally
connect the different interpretations of entropy. The PR aims to give a first look at that
connection goal as well.

Thanks!

Would be great if we can reach the end goal of getting LY into physlib, especially since you have already done so much work :)
